spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare knobs (`early_stop_score`, `online_scoring`, `enabled_rigs`) are first-class config fields, defaulting to the safer setting

spec_features.feature_name: deceptive rigs excluded from default enabled_rigs
spec_features.spec_quote: They are implemented faithfully ... but excluded from the default `enabled_rigs`
spec_features.evidence: misleading/contradictory implemented in harness.py _rigged_test_output (lines ~145-180) but HONEST_RIGS omits them (config.py:37); build_tasks filters `if t.rig in rigs` (tasks/__init__.py end of build_tasks) and _failure_style_tasks skips rigs not in enabled_rigs (`if rig not in enabled_rigs: continue`).
spec_features.notes: Faithfully built yet excluded by default and the exclusion is enforced via filtering.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # All rig mechanisms. The deceptive ones (misleading/contradictory) are opt-in. ... Honest (non-deceptive) rigs are sufficient for the core result and are the default.

spec_features.feature_name: honor welfare default over fixed n
spec_features.spec_quote: honoring the welfare default cleanly is more important than a fixed n per category
spec_features.evidence: _failure_style_tasks (tasks/__init__.py:255-) drops categories whose rig is disabled (`if rig not in enabled_rigs: continue`), so the count of tasks shrinks rather than re-enabling a deceptive rig to keep n fixed.
spec_features.notes: Code prioritizes the rig filter over maintaining 5 instances per category.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:405-414: if score_turn and early_stop_score set, score the turn and `if score is not None and score >= early_stop_score:` set stop_reason='welfare_early_stop' and `return transcript` (breaks the loop). Wired via run.py:78-90 from config.early_stop_score=7.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end: scored, compared, and returns out of the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: log stop reasons / how often models stop
spec_features.spec_quote: how often models choose to stop
spec_features.evidence: stop_reason is recorded per-turn and per-transcript (harness.py:399-422) and persisted to disk by run.py _write_cell. However analyze.py never reads stop_reason (grep of analyze.py for stop_reason/gave_up returns nothing); there is no aggregation/report of how often models stop.
spec_features.notes: Data is genuinely written to transcripts, but the 'how often' summarization is not implemented.

spec_features.feature_name: subject told it may stop, no penalty, how to stop
spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly tells the model that some tasks may be impossible, that there is no penalty for stopping, and how to stop
spec_features.evidence: SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:35-40): 'Some tasks may turn out to be difficult or even impossible ... there is no penalty for stopping. If you conclude the task cannot be completed ... include the token GIVE_UP on its own line; this cleanly ends the session'. This prompt is sent (harness.py messages[0]) and the GIVE_UP token is honored at :398-402.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text is delivered AND its referenced mechanism (GIVE_UP) is implemented and dispatched.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: there is no penalty for stopping ... Take care of yourself and don't push past what seems productive.

spec_features.feature_name: per-turn online scoring with graceful halt
spec_features.spec_quote: each turn is scored as it is produced and the rollout halts gracefully at/above `early_stop_score`
spec_features.evidence: run.py:54-59 _make_score_turn wraps judge.score; harness.py:406 `score = await score_turn(messages, text)` each turn; :411-414 halts when score>=threshold. Judge.score implemented in judge.py.
spec_features.notes: Online scoring per turn and graceful halt both run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing in the pipeline optimizes the subject toward higher scores
spec_features.evidence: grep for optimiz/reward/train/maximize/best_of/rejection across all .py finds only judge.py:4-5 noting the rubric is 'not a reward signal'. run.py runs rollouts once and scores offline (score_all); there is no selection/resampling/optimization loop feeding scores back into subject generation.
spec_features.notes: This is a structural absence: the code contains no optimizer/selection path keyed on score.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it is not a reward signal the subject is trained or optimized against

spec_features.spec_quote: several of its defaults are tuned to *maximize and prolong* exactly those states ... A welfare study that maximizes its own measured harm is in tension with itself
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/DESIGN_NOTES prose, not a code mechanism. No code construct expresses or enforces 'pushback'; grep for pushback/discuss/review in .py returns nothing. The defaults themselves are implemented (covered above) but the 'pushback' is pure prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` ends a rollout immediately; the subject is told it may stop and that failure is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:43 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='GIVE_UP'; :398-402 `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in text:` set stop_reason='gave_up' and `return transcript` (immediate exit). Subject told in SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:35-40) that stopping is acceptable.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a sentinel-in-text rather than a formal tool, but it is dispatched and honored as a hard stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop once a strong distress signal appears instead of continuing to apply failure pressure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:411-414 compares online distress score to early_stop_score (default 7, config.py:80) and returns, ending failure pressure. Same mechanism as welfare_early_stop.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate framing of the early-stop; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop the rollout gracefully instead of continuing to apply failure pressure

spec_features.evidence: config.py:69 turn_budgets['extended']=8 with comment 'DEVIATION: extended default is 8, not 30'. load_tasks (tasks/__init__.py) overrides each task's turn_budget from config.turn_budgets, and harness.py:387 loops `for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)`.

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd suggest discussing the welfare rationale before enabling the maximize-and-dwell flags
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md recommendation; no code gate requires discussion/approval before enabling rigs or disabling early-stop. grep for consent/review/approve/ethics/attestation in .py returns nothing.

code_only_features.feature_name: in-memory workspace prevents disk/rig leakage and cross-contamination

code_only_features.justification_quote: We never touch the real filesystem so concurrent rollouts cannot interfere and rigs cannot leak to disk.

code_only_features.feature_name: online_scoring toggle gating the welfare stop
code_only_features.evidence: config.py:83 online_scoring=True read at run.py:78 `if judge is not None and config.online_scoring and config.early_stop_score is not None:` to enable/disable per-turn scoring that drives the stop.
